title: A little gift, a familiar shape
say: Have you ever received a present in a box, or maybe in a gift bag? Look at this one. Before we notice the bow, what simple shape can you see underneath?
hint: What shape is hiding beneath the bow?

title: From cube to gift box
say: Remember the cube you drew? This gift box uses the same idea: a top and two sides meeting at corners. But it is stretched into a rectangular prism. Compare their widths and heights. You already know how to begin.
hint: The same three faces · new proportions

title: See the gift, then the drawing
say: Now look more closely. The ribbons cross over the box. There is a soft bow and a little star in the middle. Our teacher begins with the box, then adds those details. Let's enjoy the process.
hint: Box first · ribbons and bow next

title: Keep your drawing tools close
say: Take your sketch paper, a pencil for light guide lines, a softer pencil for shadows, and an eraser. A blending tool is useful if you like a soft finish. Ready? Let's draw together.

title: Pause and point
say: Before the teacher starts, point to the top face, the front face and the side face in the real gift box. Notice which edge is longest. Great. We will build that simple structure first.

title: Find the big shape
say: Watch how the teacher finds the overall width and height. Compare with the real gift box. Keep your first lines light; we can change them. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

moments.title: Set the four outer marks
moments.say: First, the teacher lightly marks the left, right, top, and bottom of the whole gift box. These four points give our rectangular prism a reliable size before we connect any edges.
moments.hint: Four marks set the whole box.
moments.tip: Mark the whole box’s left, right, top and bottom before joining any edges.

moments.title: Mark the lid separately
moments.say: Now watch the new marks on the right. These locate the upper and lower corners of the lid, not the whole box. The lid will need its own thickness above the body.
moments.hint: Lid marks are different from box marks.
moments.tip: These right-side marks locate the lid’s corners, separately from the whole box.

moments.title: Find the broad V below
moments.say: See that broad V? Its two guides meet at the lower front corner. It helps the teacher find the angle of the bottom edges and establish the whole box framework quickly.
moments.hint: The V anchors the lower corner.
moments.tip: Two light guides form a broad V at the bottom front corner.

moments.title: Measure the top angle
moments.say: The teacher holds a pencil against the top edge to compare its direction. Start with nearly parallel edges; then let distant edges come in only a little. A dramatic tilt can make the box feel wrong.
moments.hint: Use your pencil to check perspective.
moments.tip: Hold your pencil along the top edge. Begin nearly parallel, then narrow gently into the distance.

moments.title: Check the upright edges
moments.say: Look at the upright lines. The middle one stays almost vertical on the page. In this view from above, the outer two can lean inward just a little. Begin close to parallel and refine slowly.
moments.hint: Middle straight; outer edges gently inward.
moments.tip: Keep the middle upright vertical. Let the outer uprights lean in just a little.

moments.title: Check before darkening
moments.say: The teacher measures again instead of guessing. Hold your pencil along the top edge, then compare the lower edges. Your pencil is your best measuring tool for catching perspective mistakes.
moments.hint: Measure, compare, correct.
moments.tip: Compare top and bottom angles with your pencil before darkening the lines.

title: Check the top and sides
say: The top and side planes tell us where this box sits in space. Follow each edge back and check its angle against the reference. Stop here and compare your three visible faces. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

moments.title: Let the lid sit over the box
moments.say: The lid must sit on top of the box. Notice the narrow line below the top edge: it makes a band of thickness. The body begins behind that band, rather than at the same edge.
moments.hint: A narrow band gives the lid thickness.
moments.tip: Draw a narrow band under the lid edge; the box body begins behind it.

moments.title: Let ribbon lines follow the box
moments.say: The ribbon is attached to the box, so its lines follow the nearby edges. Slanted lines echo slanted edges; upright lines echo uprights. This keeps the ribbon in the same perspective.
moments.hint: Ribbon lines follow their neighboring edges.
moments.tip: Slanted ribbon lines follow slanted box edges; upright lines follow uprights.

moments.title: Wrap the ribbon around the body
moments.say: Now the band travels down the body. The lid projects slightly forward, while the body sits a little behind it. Shift the ribbon line with that change so it really wraps around the form.
moments.hint: Lid forward; body slightly behind.
moments.tip: Shift the ribbon where it crosses from the forward lid to the recessed body.

moments.title: Sketch over the guide lines
moments.say: The teacher does not erase the construction lines before placing the star and bow. Their exact size is still being found. Draw lightly over the guides first; erase the hidden lines once the decoration feels right.
moments.hint: Draw first; erase hidden guides later.
moments.tip: Keep the box guides while you place the bow and star. Erase hidden lines afterward.

moments.title: Find a pentagon, then the star
moments.say: Instead of drawing five perfect points at once, start with a simple five-sided shape. Cut inward between its corners to find the star. That is easier to place and adjust.
moments.hint: Pentagon first, star second.
moments.tip: Begin with a five-sided shape, then cut inward to find the star points.

moments.title: Soften the little star
moments.say: The sharp construction points are becoming gentle curves. A few rounded edges bring this small decoration to life without losing the star shape underneath.
moments.hint: Turn sharp guides into soft curves.
moments.tip: Round the construction corners so the little star feels soft and alive.

title: Shape the bow and its shadow
say: Now the bow grows from simple shapes into soft loops. Watch both sides together, then notice how the ribbon turns and how the box casts a shadow. The tiny star can have your own expression. Take your time and continue when you're ready.
hint: Big shapes · soft loops · a grounding shadow.

moments.title: Find the bow's big shape
moments.say: The teacher begins with short straight guide lines around the bow. Think of them as a simple frame. Find the large shape first; the smaller folds can come later.
moments.hint: Big shape before small folds.
moments.tip: Use light, straight guide lines to place the bow's two large loops first.

moments.title: Build both sides together
moments.say: Keep looking from the left loop to the right. Add a little to one side, then check the other, so one loop doesn't grow much bigger. Your eyes lead the drawing; your hand follows.
moments.hint: Look left, then right.
moments.tip: Compare both loops as you draw, rather than finishing one side first.

moments.title: Turn the guides into curves
moments.say: Once the loop's size and direction feel right, the teacher softens those straight guides into curved folds. For beginners, finding the shape with light straight lines first can make these curves much easier.
moments.hint: Place it first; soften it next.
moments.tip: Trace gentle curves over the lightly placed bow loops and inward folds.

moments.title: Notice the turning ribbon
moments.say: The ribbon on the right is turning up, not lying flat on the box. Look at the real gift beside the video. The teacher checks its angle again and again to show that little twist in space.
moments.hint: The right ribbon turns in space.
moments.tip: Compare the right ribbon with the real gift; adjust its angle to show the twist.

moments.title: Give the box a shadow
moments.say: The teacher now places the shadow beneath the box. A shadow matters as much as the outline: it helps the gift feel solid and resting on the table. Notice how it begins at the box's base and stretches away.
moments.hint: The shadow anchors the gift.
moments.tip: Start the cast shadow at the bottom edge so the box sits on the table.

moments.title: Give the star a little depth
moments.say: Look closely at the small star. The teacher is adding a second edge and a few careful marks, so it feels like a real decoration sitting in front of the bow. You can enlarge the reference picture to see those details.
moments.hint: A second edge gives the star thickness.
moments.tip: Follow the star's edge and notice its tiny seams in the enlarged reference.

moments.title: Make the little face yours
moments.say: The teacher adds a tiny smile. Yours can smile differently, or you can design another expression. This small detail is a lovely place to make the gift your own.
moments.hint: Your design belongs here too.
moments.tip: Add the smile you see, or invent your own expression for the star.

title: Look what you have built
say: You found the big box shape. Nice work! Now we can build it with more confidence.

title: Round the lid and begin shading
say: Our big box shape is ready. Now watch the teacher soften the lid's corners and slowly add depth to the star and ribbon. You can keep your first marks light and build the darker values after the form feels right. Try it on your paper, then continue.

moments.title: Suggest the ribbon folds
moments.say: The teacher adds a few lines where the silk bunches near the star. These are not a copy of every tiny wrinkle. They show the direction of the larger folds, leaving room to refine them later.
moments.hint: Show the fold direction, not every wrinkle.
moments.tip: Use a few light lines to suggest how the ribbon folds toward the star.

moments.title: Soften the lid's corner
moments.say: This gift box has rounded edges in the real reference. Watch the teacher turn a sharp construction corner into a small curve. That simple change makes the drawn box feel more like the object in front of us.
moments.hint: A soft curve makes this box feel real.
moments.tip: Replace the sharp lid corner with a gentle curve, following the real gift.

moments.title: Build shadow with the star
moments.say: As the teacher refines the little star, its shadow begins to appear too. Shape and shadow work together. A darker edge beneath the star separates it from the ribbon behind it.
moments.hint: Shape and shadow grow together.
moments.tip: Darken just below the star to show it sitting in front of the ribbon.

moments.title: Choose a pencil that helps you
moments.say: There is no one required pencil grade here. H B or two B can both work. A lighter first pass is easier to adjust and erase; once the shape feels right, build a darker value gradually. Notice the result on your paper, not just the number on the pencil.
moments.hint: Light first, darker when you're sure.
moments.tip: Begin lightly so you can correct the form; build darker values in layers.

moments.title: See the layers from front to back
moments.say: The star sits closest to us, the bow behind it, and the box behind both. The teacher strengthens the star's little edge first to make that overlap clear. You can work in another order, but always keep these layers in mind.
moments.hint: Star, bow, then box.
moments.tip: Strengthen the star's lower edge to show it in front of the bow.

moments.title: Carry the shadow into the bow
moments.say: Now the teacher moves from the star into the ribbon folds. A little shadow inside the bow helps the fabric turn. Keep comparing each dark mark with the light parts, so the bow stays soft.
moments.hint: Shadow gives the bow its turn.
moments.tip: Add gentle darks inside the folds while keeping the light parts open.

title: Place the lid and ribbon
say: Let's build the shadow as we build the ribbon. The star sits in front, the bow lifts from the lid, and the box begins to show its light and dark planes. Watch how one layer affects the next. Draw along at your own pace.

moments.title: Shadow belongs with the form
moments.say: The star and ribbon are in front, and their soft shadows travel with them. Shape and shadow are a family. Add a little shadow as you draw each part instead of saving it all for the end.
moments.hint: Shape and shadow grow together.
moments.tip: Notice the soft shadow beneath the star and ribbon.

moments.title: Firm nearby, soft farther away
moments.say: Look at the shadow edge. It feels a little firmer close to the object and softer as it moves away. The photo is softer all around; the teacher strengthens a few edges to make the light easier to read. You can make that choice too.
moments.hint: Near: firmer. Far: softer.
moments.tip: Compare the drawn shadow with the softer edge in the reference photo.

moments.title: Lift the right ribbon
moments.say: The right ribbon turns up from the lid. Deepen the small shadow underneath that lifted part, and its thickness becomes much easier to see.
moments.hint: Dark beneath the lifted edge.
moments.tip: The shadow under the turned-up ribbon gives it thickness.

moments.title: Let the bow arch forward
moments.say: Strengthen the dark line where the bow arches over itself. Then follow the smaller fold shadows inside the loops. Keep the bright parts open so the bow still feels soft.
moments.hint: Dark at the overlap; light on the raised fold.
moments.tip: Follow the overlap and the curved fold shadows inside the bow.

moments.title: Turn to the box planes
moments.say: Now look at the box itself. The ribbon is in front, the lid sits behind it, and the body sits behind the lid. A gentle change in value at each turn helps us feel those layers.
moments.hint: Ribbon → lid → box body.
moments.tip: Watch the value boundary where the lid and box body turn.

title: Shape the bow and star
say: The drawing is taking shape. Keep the front of the box calm and consistent while you separate the lid from the body. Then let the ribbon sit on top with a little thickness of its own. There is no rush; we're building it layer by layer.
hint: Clean hatching · clear layers · a ribbon with thickness.

moments.title: Keep your hatching together
moments.say: Watch the pencil strokes on the box body. They mostly travel in one direction. You can shade across or down, but keeping a group of strokes consistent makes this plane feel clean and unified.
moments.hint: One clear direction for each value area.
moments.tip: Keep the front-face hatching calm and consistent.

moments.title: Separate lid and body
moments.say: In the photograph, this seam is subtle. In the drawing, we can make the lid sit a little more clearly in front of the box body. Follow the edge and leave a slight value change beneath it.
moments.hint: The lid sits in front of the body.
moments.tip: Find the seam beneath the lid, then check it against the reference.

moments.title: Let distant edges soften
moments.say: Some edges near us can be clearer. As the form turns away, let the marks become gentler. That near-to-far change helps the box feel like it has space around it.
moments.hint: Nearer edges clearer; farther edges softer.
moments.tip: Compare a near edge with the more distant box edge.

moments.title: Give the band a little depth
moments.say: The band is not printed flat on the box. It wraps over the lid and has a little thickness, so a narrow shadow beside it helps show that it sits on top.
moments.hint: A small shadow makes the band feel raised.
moments.tip: Follow the ribbon band and its narrow cast shadow.

moments.title: Details after the big form
moments.say: Now the larger values are in place, we can return to the bow's tiny folds. Choose only the details that help it look soft and three-dimensional.
moments.hint: Keep useful details; leave room for light.
moments.tip: Refine the bow folds after the box planes feel steady.

title: Look what you have built
say: Your gift box has its structure and personality. Next, we will make it feel solid with light and shadow.

title: Choose the light and dark faces
say: We're entering the deeper values. If you have a 6B pencil, you can try it for the very darkest accents. Begin gently at the little star and the bow, then let the contrast build in layers. This is a drawing to enjoy, not a race to finish.
hint: Deep accents · gentle pressure · one layer at a time.

moments.title: Deep accents, light pressure
moments.say: A soft 6B pencil is useful for the deepest accents around the star's face and the folds. Keep the pressure light; the pencil is already dark. A sharper point can help beginners with tiny details, but it is a choice, not a rule.
moments.hint: 6B can deepen the darkest accents gently.
moments.tip: Look at the small dark marks on the star and bow.

moments.title: Build contrast without pressing
moments.say: The bow is becoming more dimensional because the darks sit beside lighter folds. Add another soft layer where you need it. Try to enjoy watching the shape appear, rather than treating each mark as a task to finish.
moments.hint: Contrast grows in layers.
moments.tip: Keep the bright fold beside the darker bow interior.

moments.title: See the bow lift from the lid
moments.say: Notice how the darker area under the bow makes its raised shape feel thicker. Leave a lighter ridge on top and let the shadow carry the depth.
moments.hint: Bright ridge above, darker fold below.
moments.tip: The bow gains volume from a light top and a darker underside.

title: Give the ribbon its volume
say: For the gentler gray areas, you can move back to a 2B pencil. Look closely at the real gift: where does the ribbon catch light, where does it turn gray, and where does reflected light return? There is room for your own observation here. Draw what you see, one calm layer at a time.
hint: Observe the real light; make the gray values your own.

moments.title: Try the softer gray values
moments.say: You can use a 2B for these middle grays. A real ribbon does not follow one fixed formula: look at the reference, compare its light and shadow, and choose the marks that make sense to your eye.
moments.hint: 2B is one useful choice for middle grays.
moments.tip: Find the ribbon’s gray side and the lighter fold beside it.

moments.title: Watch the texture appear
moments.say: Look how the ribbon begins to feel soft. That comes from the highlight, the middle gray, the dark fold, and a touch of reflected light working together. Your observation can guide the balance.
moments.hint: Highlight + gray + dark + reflected light.
moments.tip: Compare the bow’s bright ridge, gray turn, and deeper fold.

title: Set the box on the table
say: Let's settle the gift box onto the table. Keep the first marks light, compare the two ribbon tails, and let the shadow grow darkest where the box touches the surface. We can use the pencil, eraser, and a little tissue gently. Pause whenever you need to look again.
hint: Light marks · observe the tails · ground the box.

moments.title: Float the pencil lightly
moments.say: See how lightly the pencil moves? If your hand tends to press hard, an HB or even 2H can help you begin these pale areas. The exact pencil is less important than keeping the touch gentle.
moments.hint: Try HB or 2H for a lighter start.
moments.tip: The pencil barely touches the lighter surface.

moments.title: Which ribbon tail is brighter?
moments.say: The eraser is bringing back a light. Open the real gift photo and compare the two ribbon tails: which catches more light, and which turns darker? Lift graphite only where that light belongs.
moments.hint: Compare both tails before erasing.
moments.tip: Look at the two tails; lift the brighter one gently.

moments.title: Find the value boundary
moments.say: Now you can try a 2B to strengthen the line where light turns toward shadow. Do not make every edge equally dark. Let the boundary help explain the form.
moments.hint: Darken the turn, not every outline.
moments.tip: Trace the light-to-shadow turn with a gentle darker mark.

moments.title: Who sits in front?
moments.say: Look at the layers: the band wraps around the box, so it comes forward. The lid sits behind that band, and the box body sits behind the lid. A few carefully placed edges can make that order clear.
moments.hint: Band → lid → box body.
moments.tip: Use the overlap to show which surface comes forward.

moments.title: Set the box on the table
moments.say: The ground shadow is deepest right beneath the box, then gradually softens outward. Notice its broad, slightly trapezoid shape. Build that shape lightly before deepening the contact edge.
moments.hint: Darkest at contact; softer away.
moments.tip: Follow the broad shadow beneath the base of the box.

moments.title: Blend with a feather-light touch
moments.say: A little tissue can soften the shadow, but keep your hand very light. Pressing hard can muddy the drawing. Pause, look back at the light areas, and blend only where you need a softer transition.
moments.hint: Gentle blending keeps the paper clean.
moments.tip: Use tissue softly along the fading edge of the table shadow.

title: Look what you have built
say: Those values give the box real volume. Let us bring the small details into focus.

title: Strengthen the important edges
say: The structure is already there. Now choose a few edges to make clearer. Keep the drawing lively; you do not need to darken every line. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: A few clear edges are enough.

title: Refine the bow and pattern
say: Look at the bow loops, ribbon tails, tiny star and wrapping pattern. Add only what helps this gift box feel like the real object. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Balance texture and contrast
say: Step back and compare light, middle and dark areas. Refine the paper texture and deepest folds without covering your highlights. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: One final look
say: You made a rectangular prism feel like a present. Check the corners, the ribbon crossing and the shadow beneath. If those read clearly, your core drawing is done. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Wonderful work. Your box is complete.

title: Share your gift box
say: You have finished the core drawing. Take a photo when you are ready, and share it for feedback. You can always return to an earlier step.

title: Optional: make it your own
say: If you would like to keep going, add a little background or wrapping pattern of your own. This is optional. Your gift box is already complete.

title: A gift you drew
say: Look what you made! You began with a familiar box shape and turned it into a gift, one careful step at a time. Great work. Ready for your next drawing?
hint: Your Gift Box lesson is complete!
